evidence: src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: constructor injects `@InjectRepository(CourseEntity) private readonly courseRepository: Repository<CourseEntity>`, which is another module's persistence entity
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts: `import { toCourse } from '../courses/courses.service'` pulls an internal mapper out of another service instead of using the courses module's service API
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `course.admit(); entity.enrolled = course.enrolled; await courseRepository.save(entity);` writes the course aggregate back by hand
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `const courseRepository = this.courseRepository;` is a local alias that hides the direct use of the course repository
src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts enrol(): `if (!studentEmail.includes('@')) throw new DomainError('invalid', ...)` puts the enrolment invariant in the service, not in the Enrolment domain object

src/enrolments/enrolments.service.ts withdraw(): `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)` maps by hand, while enrol() uses `create({ ...enrolment })` and courses use a `toCourse` mapper
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is a single file, enrolments.service.ts. Enrolling and withdrawing are one cohesive concern. The problem is that `enrol` also runs and saves the course's capacity change itself. It injects `Repository<CourseEntity>`, pulls the row and the free function `toCourse` out of courses.service.ts, calls `course.admit()`, copies the counter back with `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled` and saves through `courseRepository.save(entity)`. Two things follow. First, the course-aggregate write-back rule now lives in this file as well as in the courses module, so it exists in two places. Second, the courses module's own service abstraction is skipped in favour of its internal mapper and its persistence entity; the local alias `const courseRepository = this.courseRepository` only hides this. The file is also inconsistent about domain mapping. Courses go through a mapper (`toCourse`). Enrolments are built by hand: `new Enrolment(row.courseId, row.studentEmail, row.enrolledAt)` when reading, and `create({ ...enrolment })` when saving. Finally, the email invariant (`studentEmail.includes('@')`) is written inline in the service rather than in the `Enrolment` domain object, so other paths that create an `Enrolment` can skip it. I can't confirm the courses-side duplication without seeing courses.service.ts, which is why confidence is moderate.

violations.message: enrol() skips the courses module's abstraction. It injects Repository<CourseEntity>, imports the internal `toCourse` mapper from courses.service, calls course.admit(), copies `entity.enrolled = course.enrolled` and saves the course row itself. The course capacity and write-back rule now lives in two places instead of only in the courses module.

Abstractions are used inconsistently. The student-email invariant is checked inline in the service rather than in the Enrolment domain object. Enrolment rows are mapped by hand (`new Enrolment(row.courseId, ...)` and `create({ ...enrolment })`), while courses go through a mapper.
